summary: The prepared base already supports MXFP6 E2M3 as the A operand and passes its GPU regressions. Candidate 9bf7434049ef10ebc0329f1f3567b961aee73f0b changes only the test oracle; its independent bit-level decoders are correct and all candidate and adversarial GPU checks pass. It is useful test hardening, but it is not the production fix for the original missing-support report.

tests.what_was_measured: All 10 existing MXFP6-A/MXFP4-B GPU cases passed on the prepared base with unchanged rtol=0.1 and atol=0.1.
All 10 cases passed against the candidate's independent packed-value decoder for bf16 and fp16 output.

tests.command: standalone exhaustive E2M3 pack/decode and padding-independence check
tests.what_was_measured: All 64 FP6 codes matched a direct mathematical reference exactly (max absolute error 0.0), and changing padding bytes did not change decoded values.

tests.command: direct candidate test calls for M={1,31,32,33}, N=128, K=256, output={bf16,fp16}
tests.what_was_measured: Eight GPU row/tile-boundary cases passed. Seeded M=33 bf16: max_abs=0.125, max_rel=0.0038910506, mean_abs=0.0173192 with unchanged rtol=0.1 and atol=0.1.
Fresh gfx950 compilation and execution passed; final ISA targets gfx950 and contains v_mfma_scale_f32_16x16x128_f8f6f4.

gpu_execution_evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) executed the base, exact candidate, boundary, numeric, and ISA-dump regressions successfully.
remaining_limitations: Only gfx950 was verified. The historical post-f5c50f4 failure was not reconstructed because the prepared base already has MXFP6-A support. Native libraries remained the pinned wheel at /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flydsl/_mlir because the candidate has no native C++ changes. Raw evidence is retained at /job/review-evidence.
